metadata.description: Master Lockdown Guard Bottom in BJJ. Eddie Bravo's signature half guard variation with whip-up sweeps and Electric Chair setups. 60% sweep success rate for advanced.

overview: Lockdown Guard Bottom is Eddie Bravo's signature variation of half guard where the bottom practitioner uses a triangled leg configuration (lockdown) to control the opponent's trapped leg. This 10th Planet system position transforms traditional half guard from a stalling position into a dynamic offensive platform. The lockdown prevents the top player from completing passes while creating leverage for sweeps and back takes. By extending and controlling the trapped leg, the bottom practitioner can off-balance opponents, create angles, and attack with the whip-up, Old School sweep, and Electric Chair submissions. The position emphasizes active offense over passive defense, using the leg triangle as both a retention mechanism and an attacking lever. This position revolutionized half guard play in no-gi grappling and has become a fundamental component of modern BJJ game plans.
state_invariants: Bottom practitioner's near-side leg threads over opponent's trapped leg at knee level, then triangles back underneath the ankle, creating the lockdown configuration with ankles crossed and locked
Top practitioner's trapped leg is extended and controlled between bottom player's legs, with limited mobility and compromised base
Bottom practitioner maintains underhook on trapped-leg side or uses overhook control on far side, preventing opponent from establishing dominant crossface or underhook position
Bottom practitioner's hips remain mobile and active underneath opponent, capable of extending lockdown to off-balance or creating angular attacks
Top practitioner's weight distributed partially on bottom player's torso while struggling to maintain base against lockdown extensions and hip movements
prerequisites: Half guard position established with one opponent's leg controlled between bottom player's legs
Ability to thread near-side leg over opponent's trapped leg and triangle configuration underneath
Space to complete lockdown triangle without opponent immediately passing or extracting leg
Basic understanding of hip movement and extension mechanics for lockdown control
Opponent in range for underhook or overhook control on upper body
key_principles: Maintain tight lockdown configuration with ankles crossed and locked, using top foot to hook and extend opponent's leg
Keep lockdown active and dynamic, constantly extending and flexing to off-balance opponent and prevent base establishment
Secure underhook on trapped-leg side whenever possible for maximum control and offensive opportunities
Use hip movement to create angles toward opponent's back or to set up whip-up and Old School sweeps
Prevent opponent from getting crossface control by using frames, overhooks, or underhook dominance
Stay active with attacks and sweeps rather than holding static position, forcing opponent to defend
Coordinate lockdown extensions with upper body movements to multiply off-balancing effects

common_errors.error: Locking lockdown too loosely, allowing opponent to easily extract trapped leg
common_errors.consequence: Opponent escapes half guard and completes pass to side control or mount
common_errors.correction: Cross ankles tightly with top foot hooking deep under opponent's ankle, squeeze knees together to create maximum pressure on trapped leg

common_errors.error: Remaining static in lockdown without extending or attacking, allowing opponent to establish dominant grips
common_errors.consequence: Opponent secures crossface and underhook control, nullifying lockdown's offensive potential and setting up pass
common_errors.correction: Constantly move hips, extend lockdown to off-balance opponent, and immediately attack with sweeps when opponent adjusts base

common_errors.error: Failing to fight for underhook on trapped-leg side, allowing opponent free underhook
common_errors.consequence: Opponent uses underhook to flatten bottom player, establish crossface, and systematically break down lockdown for pass
common_errors.correction: Prioritize underhook battle, use frames and overhooks when underhook unavailable, never allow opponent free underhook without immediate counter

common_errors.error: Extending lockdown without coordinating upper body attack or sweep attempt
common_errors.consequence: Opponent anticipates lockdown extension, times extraction or pass, and escapes without significant difficulty
common_errors.correction: Coordinate lockdown extensions with upper body movements, attack combinations (extend while setting up Old School or whip-up), making extensions purposeful rather than random

common_errors.error: Allowing opponent to establish strong crossface without defensive response
common_errors.consequence: Opponent flattens bottom player completely, eliminates lockdown's effectiveness, and completes pass to side control
common_errors.correction: Immediately counter crossface with frames, overhook, or whip-up movement to prevent flattening, maintain ability to turn into opponent

common_errors.error: Attempting Electric Chair or Old School without proper setup and angle creation
common_errors.consequence: Opponent defends sweep or submission easily, potentially counters with pass or dominant position
common_errors.correction: Create proper angles with hip movement before committing to attacks, use lockdown extensions to off-balance first, then enter sweeps and submissions with timing

training_drills.name: Lockdown Retention Drill
training_drills.description: Partner attempts to extract trapped leg using various methods (pulling back, driving forward, underhook pressure) while bottom player maintains lockdown integrity and counters extraction attempts. Focus on keeping ankles locked, extending strategically, and preventing leg escape. Duration: 3-5 minutes per round, switching roles.

training_drills.name: Whip-up to Old School Combination Drill
training_drills.description: From established lockdown, bottom player practices transitioning between whip-up and Old School sweep based on opponent's reactions. If opponent bases out against whip-up, switch to Old School. If opponent sits back against Old School, switch to whip-up. Develop timing and recognition of sweep opportunities. Duration: 5 minutes per round.

training_drills.name: Lockdown to Electric Chair Progression
training_drills.description: Starting from lockdown with underhook, practice full Electric Chair entry sequence: extend opponent's leg with lockdown, rotate to outside, establish lockdown triangle in Electric Chair configuration, and apply submission pressure. Partner provides progressive resistance. Duration: 5-7 minutes per round.

training_drills.name: Underhook Battle from Lockdown
training_drills.description: Both partners fight for underhook control while bottom player maintains lockdown. Top player attempts to strip underhook and establish crossface, bottom player recovers underhook and prevents flattening. Emphasizes grip fighting and positional maintenance under pressure. Duration: 3-5 minutes per round.

training_drills.name: Positional Sparring: Lockdown vs. Pass
training_drills.description: Bottom player starts in lockdown with underhook, top player attempts to pass. Bottom player scores points for sweeps and submissions, top player scores for passes and dominant positions. Resets after each score. Develop competitive timing and strategy. Duration: 5-10 minute rounds.

expert_insights.danaher: The lockdown represents a fundamental shift in half guard philosophy from purely defensive retention to active offensive control. By creating a mechanical advantage through the triangled leg configuration, the bottom practitioner transforms the opponent's trapped leg into a lever system that can be extended, retracted, and manipulated to generate off-balancing forces. The biomechanical principle at work is simple: when you control an opponent's base through their leg and can extend or compress that leg at will, you create instability that opens opportunities for sweeps and positional advances. The lockdown's effectiveness stems from its ability to simultaneously limit the opponent's mobility while maximizing your own offensive options. However, practitioners must understand that the lockdown is not a static holding position but rather a dynamic control platform that requires constant adjustment, extension timing, and coordination with upper body attacks to be effective at high levels.
expert_insights.gordon_ryan: In competition, the lockdown can be an extremely effective tool when used with aggressive intent and proper timing, but it requires complete commitment to the position's offensive nature. I've seen too many competitors use lockdown passively, simply holding and waiting, which allows elite passers to systematically break it down and complete passes. The key to competitive success with lockdown is maintaining constant pressure through extensions, immediately attacking with sweeps when opponents adjust their base, and never allowing them to establish both crossface and underhook control simultaneously. The whip-up and Old School sweeps are high-percentage techniques that work even against world-class opponents if you commit fully and time them with the opponent's weight shifts. The Electric Chair is a legitimate submission threat that forces opponents to defend, opening other opportunities. The lockdown works best when you treat it as a launching pad for attacks rather than a defensive bunker, making it a viable option even at the highest levels of no-gi competition.
expert_insights.eddie_bravo: The lockdown is the foundation of the entire 10th Planet half guard system and represents a complete reimagining of what half guard can be. Traditional half guard was always seen as a stalling position or a last resort before getting passed, but the lockdown transforms it into one of the most dynamic and dangerous positions in all of grappling. When you lock down that leg and start extending, you're not just preventing passes—you're actively attacking, creating dilemmas, and forcing your opponent to make difficult choices under pressure. The beauty of the lockdown is how it chains into so many different attacks: the Old School sweep, the whip-up, the Electric Chair, transitions to the truck, and numerous other options. The position rewards creativity and aggression, allowing smaller practitioners to control and sweep much larger opponents through leverage rather than strength. The key is staying active, constantly moving your hips, extending that lockdown to off-balance them, and immediately attacking when they react. The lockdown isn't just a technique—it's a complete game plan that can carry you through entire matches if you commit to mastering its intricacies and developing the timing to execute its attacks under pressure.

metadata.title: Lockdown Guard | BJJ Position Guide | BJJ Graph
metadata.description: Master Lockdown Guard in BJJ. 10th Planet half guard control system with leg entanglement. High-percentage sweeps and back takes with 65% sweep success at advanced level.

overview:
Lockdown Guard is a specialized half guard variation developed and popularized by Eddie Bravo as a cornerstone of the 10th Planet Jiu-Jitsu system. This position features a unique leg entanglement where the bottom player's outside leg triangles around the opponent's trapped leg, creating a lockdown configuration that severely restricts the top player's mobility and base. The position transforms traditional half guard from a defensive holding pattern into an aggressive attacking platform, offering powerful sweeps, back takes, and submission opportunities.

The lockdown mechanism works by using the bottom player's outside leg to hook under the opponent's shin while the inside leg wraps over the thigh, creating a figure-four leg lock around the trapped limb. This configuration prevents the top player from completing traditional half guard passes, as they cannot free their leg to establish side control or mount. The bottom player gains tremendous leverage to break the opponent's posture, manipulate their weight distribution, and create angles for offensive attacks. The position is particularly effective in no-gi grappling where traditional gi grips are unavailable.

Within the 10th Planet system, Lockdown Guard serves as the foundation for multiple attacking sequences, including the Electric Chair sweep, Old School sweep, and various paths to the back. The position emphasizes constant pressure and movement, using the lockdown to control distance while working toward dominant positions. When executed with proper technique and understanding of the system's principles, Lockdown Guard becomes a highly effective tool for smaller practitioners to neutralize larger opponents and create offensive opportunities from what appears to be a defensive bottom position.

Top player's posture compromised by lockdown tension, forcing them to deal with leg entanglement before attempting traditional passing sequences

Use lockdown to break opponent's posture by extending hips away while pulling trapped leg
Control opponent's upper body with underhook or whip-up to prevent crossface and flatten attempts

common_errors.error: Failing to maintain constant tension in the lockdown, allowing opponent to free their leg
common_errors.consequence: Opponent escapes lockdown and completes traditional half guard pass to side control
common_errors.correction: Continuously pull opponent's heel toward your hip while flexing outside foot, maintaining figure-four pressure throughout all movements

common_errors.error: Allowing opponent to establish crossface control and flatten you to the mat
common_errors.consequence: Loss of mobility and offensive options, making it difficult to create angles for sweeps or attacks
common_errors.correction: Secure underhook or whip-up immediately, frame against opponent's head and shoulder, and stay on your side to maintain attacking posture

common_errors.error: Staying static in lockdown without progressing to offensive techniques
common_errors.consequence: Opponent adjusts their base and finds solutions to the lockdown, eventually passing or stalling for referee intervention
common_errors.correction: Constantly work toward Old School, Electric Chair, or other attacking sequences, using lockdown as control mechanism not end goal

common_errors.error: Attempting to finish Electric Chair or Old School without proper setup and angle creation
common_errors.consequence: Techniques fail and opponent capitalizes on failed attempt to establish superior position
common_errors.correction: Break opponent's posture first with lockdown, create necessary angles by shrimping and underhook control, then execute technique with proper timing

common_errors.error: Locking down too high on opponent's leg (around knee instead of shin)
common_errors.consequence: Reduced leverage and control, allowing opponent to maintain better posture and potentially escape
common_errors.correction: Ensure outside leg hooks deep under opponent's shin, close to the ankle, maximizing leverage and control of trapped leg

common_errors.error: Neglecting to control opponent's upper body while focusing only on lockdown
common_errors.consequence: Opponent uses free upper body to establish dominant grips, crossface, and eventually break lockdown
common_errors.correction: Maintain constant upper body control through underhook, overhook, or whip-up while simultaneously managing lockdown

common_errors.error: Releasing lockdown too early when transitioning to other positions
common_errors.consequence: Loss of control advantage and opponent immediately establishes superior position or completes pass
common_errors.correction: Maintain lockdown until you have secured alternate control (back control grips, deep half hooks, etc.) during transitions

training_drills.name: Lockdown Maintenance Drill
training_drills.description: Partner takes top half guard position. Bottom player establishes lockdown and maintains control for 2-minute rounds while top player attempts to free their leg using various escape methods. Focus on maintaining constant tension and preventing leg extraction. Switch roles and repeat for 5 rounds.

training_drills.name: Old School Sweep Flow Drill
training_drills.description: From established lockdown, practice Old School sweep sequence in repetitions of 10. Partner provides progressive resistance: first static (no resistance), then moderate resistance, finally full resistance. Focus on proper angle creation, underhook control, and hip extension timing. Perform 3 sets of 10 repetitions per side.

training_drills.name: Electric Chair Setup and Finish Drill
training_drills.description: Partner in top half guard. Bottom player secures lockdown and practices Electric Chair setup by breaking posture, creating angle, and securing proper leg position. Practice both submission finish and sweep option. Partner taps to calf pressure. Perform 5 successful setups per side, alternating between submission and sweep finish.

training_drills.name: Lockdown to Back Take Transition Drill
training_drills.description: From lockdown position, practice multiple pathways to back control including rolling back take and truck transition. Partner provides realistic resistance but allows completion of technique when properly executed. Focus on maintaining lockdown control throughout transition and only releasing when back control is secure. 3-minute rounds for 4 rounds.

training_drills.name: Lockdown Defense and Recovery Drill
training_drills.description: Partner establishes lockdown. Top player practices various defense and escape methods (posture maintenance, leg extraction, base widening) while bottom player maintains control and looks for opportunities to advance. Emphasizes problem-solving for both positions. 3-minute rounds, switching roles after each round for 6 total rounds.

expert_insights.danaher: The lockdown represents a fascinating biomechanical puzzle that Eddie Bravo solved through systematic analysis of half guard control mechanisms. By creating a figure-four configuration around the opponent's trapped leg, the bottom player generates asymmetrical control that fundamentally disrupts the top player's ability to establish the bilateral base required for effective passing. The genius of the position lies in how it transforms defensive half guard into an offensive platform by controlling the opponent's center of gravity through their trapped leg while simultaneously limiting their ability to generate forward pressure. The lockdown creates what I call 'positional debt' where the top player must solve the leg entanglement problem before they can even begin addressing traditional half guard passing concepts, effectively adding an entire layer of complexity to their task.
expert_insights.gordon_ryan: In no-gi competition, lockdown is one of the highest percentage half guard systems available because it removes so many of the top player's options immediately. When I'm on top against a good lockdown player, I know I'm in for a tough time because the leg control is so dominant that my usual passing chains don't work. The key to making lockdown work at the highest level is being genuinely dangerous with your attacks—if your Electric Chair, Old School, and back takes are serious threats, the top player has to respect them, which opens up even more opportunities. I've seen too many people just lock it down and stall, which doesn't work against good opponents who know the defenses. You need to be constantly attacking and making them react, using the lockdown as the control mechanism that enables your offense rather than the attack itself.
expert_insights.eddie_bravo: I developed the lockdown system because traditional half guard was too passive and defensive for my style—I wanted a half guard that let me attack constantly and put the top guy in immediate danger. The lockdown solves the fundamental problem of half guard which is that the top guy has too much mobility and can work their passes while you're stuck defending. By locking down their leg, you flip the script completely and now they're the ones stuck dealing with your attacks. The beauty of the system is how everything chains together: they defend the Electric Chair, you hit the Old School; they defend that, you go to the Truck; they defend the Truck, you're taking their back. It's a complete ecosystem of attacks that all stem from that initial lockdown control. People say it only works in no-gi, but that's because they haven't fully explored the system—the principles work with or without the gi if you understand the deeper concepts of leg control and weight manipulation.

overview: Lockdown Half Guard Bottom is a highly controlling half guard variation popularized by Eddie Bravo and the 10th Planet Jiu-Jitsu system. This position features a triangle-like leg configuration where the bottom player traps their opponent's leg using their own legs in a figure-four lock, creating immense control and offensive opportunities. The lockdown creates a powerful controlling mechanism that restricts the top player's mobility while enabling the bottom player to execute sweeps, transitions, and submissions. Unlike traditional half guard where the bottom player simply hooks one leg, the lockdown actively restricts the opponent's base and posture through aggressive leg entanglement. The position serves as the foundation for numerous 10th Planet techniques including the Old School Sweep, Electric Chair, and various truck entries. The lockdown's effectiveness lies in its ability to nullify the top player's passing attempts while creating powerful leverage for offensive attacks. This position represents a paradigm shift in half guard strategy, transforming a traditionally defensive position into an aggressive attacking platform.
state_invariants: Bottom player's legs create a figure-four lock around opponent's trapped leg, with one ankle crossing over the opponent's ankle and hooking behind their own knee, creating a triangle-like configuration that immobilizes the leg

Bottom player is on their side or back with the trapped opponent's leg locked between their own legs, maintaining constant inward pressure with the lockdown while controlling upper body with underhooks or overhooks

Top player's trapped leg is extended and controlled by the lockdown mechanism, with their knee pointing away from their body and their mobility severely restricted, forcing them to post their free leg wide for base

Bottom player's hips are positioned close to opponent's trapped leg with active pressure directed through the lockdown, creating leverage for sweeps while preventing the top player from extracting their leg or establishing dominant position

Hip mobility to execute the lockdown entry and maintain active pressure
key_principles: Maintain constant inward pressure with the lockdown to control opponent's posture and prevent leg extraction
Use underhooks or overhooks to control upper body and prevent opponent from flattening you with crossface pressure
Keep hips mobile and active to create angles for sweeps and prevent opponent from settling their weight
Actively extend opponent's trapped leg using the lockdown to break their base and create sweep opportunities
Combine lockdown pressure with upper body frames to maintain optimal distance and prevent being smashed flat
Use the lockdown as a platform for attacks rather than purely defensive position, constantly threatening sweeps and transitions
Control opponent's free leg and arm positioning to prevent them from establishing a strong base or passing position

common_errors.error: Allowing opponent to flatten you completely with crossface while maintaining lockdown passively
common_errors.consequence: Loss of mobility and sweep opportunities, opponent can establish dominant smash pass position despite lockdown
common_errors.correction: Immediately execute whip-up or use frames to create space when feeling crossface pressure, never accept being completely flat

common_errors.error: Failing to maintain constant inward pressure with the lockdown, allowing opponent's leg to remain mobile
common_errors.consequence: Opponent can extract their trapped leg or establish better base, negating the lockdown's controlling advantages
common_errors.correction: Actively squeeze and extend opponent's leg throughout, treating lockdown as dynamic control rather than static position

common_errors.error: Neglecting upper body control while focusing solely on the lockdown leg configuration
common_errors.consequence: Opponent can use crossface, underhook, or shoulder pressure to control your upper body and pass despite lockdown
common_errors.correction: Always combine lockdown with underhook, overhook, or whizzer control to manage opponent's upper body positioning

common_errors.error: Waiting too long to initiate sweeps, treating lockdown as purely defensive holding position
common_errors.consequence: Opponent adapts to lockdown pressure and finds passing solutions, referee may penalize for stalling
common_errors.correction: Immediately threaten old school, electric chair, or whip-up as soon as lockdown is secured to maintain offensive pressure

common_errors.error: Crossing legs too high on opponent's thigh instead of controlling the ankle/lower leg
common_errors.consequence: Weak lockdown control that opponent can easily escape, loss of leverage for sweeps and attacks
common_errors.correction: Establish figure-four lock as low as possible on opponent's leg near the ankle for maximum control and restriction

common_errors.error: Remaining static on your back without adjusting angles or creating movement
common_errors.consequence: Opponent can settle their weight and initiate passing sequences without fear of sweeps or transitions
common_errors.correction: Constantly adjust hip position, create angles with shoulder frames, and threaten multiple attacks to keep opponent defensive

training_drills.name: Lockdown Entry and Maintenance Drill
training_drills.description: From standard half guard, practice entering the lockdown by threading your bottom leg through and establishing the figure-four lock. training_drills.name: Electric Chair and Whip-Up Flow Drill

When partner posts hands and sits back, transition to electric chair. Develop ability to read opponent's weight distribution and choose appropriate attack.

expert_insights.danaher: The lockdown represents a fundamental shift in half guard philosophy from defensive holding to offensive control. The biomechanical advantage created by the figure-four leg lock around the opponent's ankle generates immense torque on their knee joint and restricts their ability to generate power through that leg. This control must be combined with systematic upper body management to prevent the opponent from using shoulder pressure and crossface control to neutralize the lockdown's advantages. The key to effective lockdown usage is understanding that the leg entanglement creates a fulcrum point around which you can generate sweeping leverage - by extending the trapped leg while controlling the upper body, you create mechanical disadvantages that even strong opponents cannot overcome through raw strength alone. The position works because it attacks multiple control points simultaneously: the trapped leg through the lockdown, the upper body through underhooks or overhooks, and the opponent's base through strategic weight displacement.
expert_insights.gordon_ryan: In competition, the lockdown is a high-percentage position when executed with the right timing and aggression. The mistake most people make is treating it like a stalling position instead of an active attacking platform. When I use lockdown, I'm immediately threatening old school sweep or electric chair - the opponent knows they're in danger and has to react, which creates openings. The lockdown works particularly well against aggressive passers who try to smash through half guard with shoulder pressure because the leg entanglement prevents them from stepping around or extracting their leg for knee slice passes. Against experienced opponents, you need to combine the lockdown with constant upper body hand fighting to prevent them from establishing dominant grips. The whip-up is crucial because it gives you an escape route when they start to figure out your lockdown attacks. I've won matches by using lockdown to slow down explosive passers and force them into my tempo, then catching sweeps when they get frustrated and make mistakes.
expert_insights.eddie_bravo: The lockdown is the foundation of the entire 10th Planet half guard system and it changed the game when we introduced it. Traditional half guard was always seen as this desperate defensive position where you're just trying to survive and maybe recover full guard. We flipped that completely - with the lockdown, you're the one in control, you're attacking, you're creating submissions. The figure-four leg lock immobilizes their leg which kills their base and makes them vulnerable to old school, electric chair, all the attacks. The beauty of the system is that everything connects - if old school doesn't work, you can hit electric chair, if that doesn't work you can whip-up to dogfight or transition to truck. It's a complete system where every position feeds into the next one. People criticize it saying you can get stuck there, but that's only if you're being passive. When you're active with the lockdown, constantly attacking, it's one of the most dominant positions in jiu-jitsu. The key is commitment - you have to be willing to extend that leg hard, create the pressure, and go for the finish. Half-ass lockdown doesn't work, but when you really crank it and combine it with upper body control, it's devastating.
